bug_semantics: ERC7984 stores confidential total supply in an euint64. On overflow, its mint path selects a transferred amount of zero and leaves supply unchanged rather than reverting. ERC7984ERC20Wrapper's wrap path first transfers the caller's underlying ERC-20 into the wrapper, while its ERC-1363 callback runs after the underlying transfer; both paths then call _mint and ignore the returned actual amount. Once the confidential supply is full, the transaction therefore succeeds with the underlying tokens retained but zero confidential wrapped tokens minted, causing user fund loss.
flaw_origin: The unsafe composition first appears in PR #11 member commit 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be: it creates ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper and adds both the transfer-then-_mint wrap path and the onTransferReceived _mint path without consuming or checking _mint's return value. The parent already had the intentionally non-reverting encrypted overflow behavior in ConfidentialFungibleToken, but had no ERC-20 wrapper, so the loss-of-funds mechanism did not yet exist.
ai_marker: absent on BIC 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be. `git cat-file -p 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be` shows human author and committer Hadrien Croubois <hadrien.croubois@gmail.com> and the sole message `Add Confidential wrapper for ERC20 tokens`; it has no AI Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailer, AI tool identity, or bot identity.
evidence: Advisory https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-confidential-contracts/security/advisories/GHSA-hqf9-8xv5-x8xw states the exact silent euint64 overflow/ignored _mint return mechanism, affected <=0.3.0, and patched 0.3.1. In the clone, `git show 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be -- contracts/token/extensions/ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper.sol` shows the new wrapper, SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom followed by unchecked _mint in wrap, and unchecked _mint in onTransferReceived. `git grep -n -C 4 -e 'function tryIncrease' -e 'function _mint' -e 'transferred = success.select' e1516e341eaae579028ab3b61523ef4d606457bc -- contracts/token/ConfidentialFungibleToken.sol` shows the pre-existing parent behavior: overflow success is computed by newValue >= oldValue, _mint returns _update, and failure selects zero. PR #11's first-party commits endpoint, https://api.github.com/repos/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-confidential-contracts/pulls/11/commits, decomposes landed squash cb6a8a7bcc27352530164817c8b68333336f22c3 into the six listed member SHAs. Across that member chain, `git log --reverse -S'_mint(to,' 214750ca57768e2ad8e22b05658d2f0e8517421a -- contracts/token/extensions/ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper.sol` and the corresponding -S'SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom' query both return 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be as the first writer; `git log -L 31,48:contracts/token/extensions/ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper.sol 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be` agrees. `git ls-tree -r e1516e341eaae579028ab3b61523ef4d606457bc -- contracts/token/extensions/ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper.sol contracts/token/ERC7984/extensions/ERC7984ERC20Wrapper.sol` is empty, directly proving parent absence. The squash landed before v0.1.0 (tag commit 71202e4b38786097fbe2e2d190940d32eda1fd69). For the closing boundary, v0.3.0 resolves to f0914b66f9f3766915403587b1ef1432d53054d3 and is the direct parent of c620d4386021dde63ae3ea1507dee8543791134a; `git show c620d4386021dde63ae3ea1507dee8543791134a` adds ERC7984TotalSupplyOverflow and an _update override that checks inferred underlying-backed supply before minting. `git grep ERC7984TotalSupplyOverflow v0.3.0 -- contracts/token/ERC7984/extensions/ERC7984ERC20Wrapper.sol` is empty, while the same query at v0.3.1 shows the error/check/override; v0.3.1 resolves to 14f20de697573d815c1bf7cd7e67f386de08707f, contains c620d4386021dde63ae3ea1507dee8543791134a, and its package.json reports 0.3.1. The same patch also landed on the mainline as 2484df01ca18fd5143dae744f46aac0bf8a2b43b, but c620d4386021dde63ae3ea1507dee8543791134a is the direct fix on the affected v0.3 release line.
reasoning: The smallest real BIC is the first PR-member commit, not GitHub's later squash object: 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be is atomic for this mechanism, its immediate parent has no wrapper, and later members only refine the newly introduced wrapper. The defect is the wrapper's failure to honor an existing zero-on-overflow _mint contract after accepting underlying assets. Commit c620d4386021dde63ae3ea1507dee8543791134a directly closes that mechanism on the vulnerable v0.3 line by making mint overflow synchronously revert, and it is included in the first patched release v0.3.1. Because the BIC commit object is authored and committed by a human and contains no qualifying AI marker, the evidence supports NOT_AI rather than either AI verdict.
